title: A case of dyskinesia after levetiracetam administration
case_prompt:
A 28-year-old woman presented with confusion after several generalized tonic-clonic seizures. She had a 4-year history of spinal cord glioblastoma with extension from the brainstem to the upper thoracic cord and a right temporal pole lesion. Two weeks earlier, her chemoradiation therapy had been completed; lumbar puncture was avoided because of intracranial mass effect. Three months prior, brain MRI confirmed tumor progression.  
On arrival she was drowsy; blood pressure was 125/65 mmHg, temperature 36.4 °C, pulse 100/min, respiratory rate 19/min. Intravenous levetiracetam, 1000 mg, was administered immediately, but she had another generalized tonic-clonic seizure without recovering consciousness. Two hours after the levetiracetam loading dose, video-EEG monitoring was started. At that time, she developed choreoathetoid movements of the face and all four limbs; concurrent EEG showed no epileptiform discharges.  
Laboratory studies, including complete blood count, electrolytes, BUN, creatinine, and ammonia, were normal. Her chronic medications—solifenacin, esomeprazole, baclofen, and escitalopram—had been unchanged for >3 months; she was not receiving dopamine-blocking or antipsychotic agents. Levetiracetam was withheld; the movements persisted for approximately 30 minutes, during which she remained alert and able to communicate.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Mesial temporal lobe seizure considered — “she was able to communicate while showing the movements, unlike mesial temporal lobe seizures in which consciousness is usually impaired.”  
2. Complex partial status epilepticus considered — “her ongoing movement did not accompany any epileptiform discharges nor clinically evolving features for a relatively long time during video-EEG monitoring, which does not meet the commonly used diagnostic criteria for CPSE.”  
3. Metabolic causes considered — “underlying metabolic causes related to chorea could be excluded by laboratory findings.”  
4. Drug–drug interactions considered — “her concomitantly administered drugs were in stable use and not generally associated with dopaminergic hyperactivity and furthermore, that LEV has pharmacokinetic drug interactions with them, we supposed that drug-to-drug interactions was not a possible mechanism.”  
5. Benzodiazepine effect considered — “Use of benzodiazepines can alleviate or terminate not only epileptic seizures but also involuntary movements such as tremor, chorea, and dystonia.”
